request_classification.request_type: documentation-wide terminology refactor with constitutional-level governance implications

claims.claim_text: Replace all occurrences of 'Layer 2' and 'Layer-2' with 'truth_store' across Documentation/ and CLAUDE.md, where the terms refer to the project's architectural layers.
claims.classification_rationale: 'Layer 2' is deeply embedded current-state terminology throughout the canonical document set. CLAUDE.md Sections 1, 3.1, 4 (Phase A), and 2.2 all use 'Layer 2' / 'Layer-2' to describe the currently operational snapshot-boundary layer. The term is verified across multiple canonical sources as referring to the current deterministic data ingestion and snapshot publication layer. The proposed rename targets current-state documentation text that describes current operational reality. This is a contract-affecting documentation change per CLAUDE.md Section 11.
notes: Layer 2 is described as 'operational at snapshot boundary' in CLAUDE.md Section 3.1 — this is current-state, not target
Phase A (Layer 2 Closure) is marked 'complete at contract boundary' in CLAUDE.md Section 4
The term appears in CLAUDE.md itself, making this a constitutional-level text modification
Section 11 document update obligations are triggered by this change

claims.claim_text: Replace all occurrences of 'Layer 3' and 'Layer-3' with 'decision_layer' across Documentation/ and CLAUDE.md, where the terms refer to the project's architectural layers.
claims.classification_rationale: Although Layer 3 refers to target architecture that is NOT YET BUILT (CLAUDE.md Section 3.2), the *terminology* 'Layer 3' / 'Layer-3' is extensively used in current canonical documentation to describe that planned architecture. CLAUDE.md Sections 3.2, 4 (Phases B/C/D), 6.1, and 10 all use 'Layer 3' as current documentation vocabulary. The claim is current-state because it modifies current documentation text — the fact that what Layer 3 *refers to* is target architecture does not change the classification of the documentation modification itself. The distinction between 'the text exists now in current docs' (current-state) and 'what the text describes is planned' (target-state) is critical. This is the former.
notes: Layer 3 components (Feature Builder, Index Suite, Regime Gate, etc.) are explicitly listed as 'planned only' in CLAUDE.md Section 3.2
The rename does not promote Layer 3 to current implementation — it changes the label used to discuss it
CLAUDE.md Section 3.2 note on Layer-2 index_suite.py ('distinct from existing Layer-2 provisional pre-publication tool') requires careful handling to avoid ambiguity under new terminology
CLAUDE.md Section 10 strong claim discipline uses 'Layer 3' — rename must preserve the prohibition semantics

claims.claim_text: The rename must be scoped strictly to architectural layer references. Unrelated literals, code module names (e.g., layer2/ directory, import paths), and historical references must not be blindly altered without governance review.
claims.classification_rationale: This constraint directly aligns with multiple CLAUDE.md governance principles: Section 2.3 (historical documents must not be used as current truth — by extension, historical references should be preserved as historical context, not silently renamed); Section 5.3 (inferred behavior does not count as proof — a term appearing in a code path does not mean it is an architectural layer reference); Section 7 (fail-closed — ambiguous cases should not be renamed). The code-conventions rule also specifies explicit imports and no hidden side effects, which a silent rename of import paths would violate. The constraint is well-grounded in current governance.
notes: The layer2/ directory path, layer2/index_suite.py, and similar code-level references are implementation artifacts with their own identity
README_LAYER2.md filename is handled separately in c4
Historical references preserved in documentation (e.g., older DecisionPacket examples in README_LAYER2.md) need case-by-case governance review

claims.claim_text: README_LAYER2.md and potentially other filenames containing 'Layer2' or 'Layer-2' may require rename handling as part of this refactor.
claims.classification_rationale: README_LAYER2.md is explicitly named in CLAUDE.md as a canonical document (Section 2.1 item 7, Section 2.2 role definition, Section 2.4 conflict resolution, Section 11 update obligations). Its filename is a constitutional-level identifier. Renaming it requires: (a) atomic update of every CLAUDE.md reference to this filename, (b) update of DOCUMENTATION_VERIFICATION_MATRIX_v1.md cross-references, (c) update of any other canonical documents that reference it by name, (d) git history considerations. This is the highest-impact sub-claim because it affects the constitutional document's own reference integrity.
notes: CLAUDE.md Section 2.1 lists 'README_LAYER2.md' by exact filename as canonical source #7
CLAUDE.md Section 2.2 defines its canonical role explicitly
CLAUDE.md Section 2.4 conflict resolution references it by filename
CLAUDE.md Section 11 references it in document update obligations
The skill doc-truth-classification Tier 3 references it by filename
Rename must be atomic across all references or it breaks canonical source resolution

claims.claim_text: The refactor must fail closed if it would introduce ambiguity, architecture drift, or snapshot-boundary confusion.
claims.classification_rationale: Directly mandated by CLAUDE.md Section 7 (fail-closed principle): 'The system MUST default to NO OUTPUT rather than incorrect output.' Applied to 'invalid states' and 'unverified assumptions.' The request's fail-closed constraint is a restatement of an existing constitutional obligation, not a new requirement. Additionally, CLAUDE.md Section 6 (snapshot contract) is non-negotiable — any rename that could blur the snapshot boundary (e.g., making it unclear which layer publishes vs. consumes snapshots) must be blocked.
notes: Architecture drift risk: if 'truth_store' is interpreted as a data store rather than a layer with specific contract obligations, the rename could subtly shift architectural semantics
Snapshot-boundary confusion risk: 'Layer 2' in CLAUDE.md Section 6 defines the snapshot publication boundary — the replacement term must preserve this semantic clarity
Ambiguity risk: 'decision_layer' could be confused with 'Decision Engine' (a specific planned component within Layer 3 per Section 3.2)

claims.claim_text: CLAUDE.md itself is explicitly in scope for the terminology changes, as stated in the request ('affecting all files under Documentation/ and CLAUDE.md').
claims.classification_rationale: CLAUDE.md is the highest-priority interpretive authority (self-declared in its preamble). It is not merely a documentation file — it is the project constitution. Modifying its terminology is a contract-affecting change that triggers the full Section 11 obligation cascade. Every section of CLAUDE.md uses 'Layer 2' and/or 'Layer 3' terminology: Sections 1, 3, 4, 6, 10, 11, and 15. The rename within CLAUDE.md must preserve all semantic invariants: phase-gate definitions, snapshot contract rules, strong claim prohibitions, evidence model constraints, and current-vs-target architecture separation.
notes: CLAUDE.md Section 3.2 contains a parenthetical clarification distinguishing Layer-2 index_suite.py from the planned Layer-3 Index Suite — this must be preserved or equivalently clarified under new terminology
CLAUDE.md Section 4 phase names reference layers — the rename must preserve phase-gate semantics
CLAUDE.md Section 10 forbidden claims reference 'Layer 3' — must remain prohibitive under new terminology
CLAUDE.md Section 6.1 'Layer 3+ MUST read ONLY from published snapshots' — semantic must be preserved exactly
This is the most governance-sensitive claim: modifying the constitutional document's own vocabulary

classification_notes.dominant_scope_rationale: All six claims are classified as current-state because the request modifies current documentation text. Although Layer 3 content refers to target architecture, the documentation modification itself is a current-state action affecting current canonical documents. The dominant scope is therefore current-state, not mixed.
key_governance_observations: This refactor is constitutional-level: it modifies the vocabulary of the project's highest-authority document (CLAUDE.md) and at least one canonical document filename (README_LAYER2.md).
The rename is terminology-only and does not claim to change architecture, implementation state, or phase status. It must be verified that the new terms preserve all existing semantic invariants.
The request's own fail-closed constraint and scope restriction (c3, c5) align with existing governance obligations and serve as additional safety rails.

The highest-risk sub-operations are: (1) renaming README_LAYER2.md with atomic cross-reference update, (2) modifying CLAUDE.md without breaking self-referential governance rules, (3) ensuring 'decision_layer' is not confused with the planned 'Decision Engine' component.
All seven canonical documents require review per CLAUDE.md Section 11, as this is a contract-affecting change.
